name: BloodHound / SharpHound Collection
description: Collect AD relationship data with SharpHound for visualization in BloodHound. Identifies attack paths to Domain Admin, unconstrained delegation hosts, and ACL misconfigurations.

steps.label: Start neo4j and BloodHound on attacker

examples.label: SharpHound stealth (exclude DCs to avoid MDI)

recommended.note: Exploit unconstrained delegation computers found in BH
Roast Kerberoastable users found in BH
Exploit WriteDACL paths found in BH

notes: Key BH queries: 'Shortest Paths to Domain Admins', 'Computers with Unconstrained Delegation', 'Find Principals with DCSync Rights'. Use --excludedcs to avoid MDI detection on DCs. Drop noisy methods (RDP, DCOM, PSRemote, LocalAdmin) for stealth - they connect to every host. LDAP-only methods (Group, GPOLocalGroup, Trusts, ACL, Container, ObjectProps, SPNTargets) are stealthiest. SOAPHound collects via ADWS (TCP 9389) instead of raw LDAP - stealthier. Build a cache first, then --bhdump.

defense.why_it_works: SharpHound queries LDAP (users, groups, GPOs, OUs, ACLs, trusts), SMB (sessions, local admin), and RPC (logged-on users) from any domain-joined host. The collected JSON feeds BloodHound's graph engine which uses Cypher queries on Neo4j to find shortest attack paths to Domain Admin - paths humans would never manually discover from raw LDAP data.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user. SharpHound.exe or SharpHound.ps1 on the target. LDAP access to DC. SMB access to enumerate session and local admin data.
defense.impact: T1087.002 Account Discovery: Domain Account + T1069.002 Permission Groups Discovery. Maps every ACL, group membership, session, and trust. Identifies shortest paths to DA via Kerberoastable accounts, GenericAll ACEs, unconstrained delegation, and more.
defense.detection:
SharpHound generates massive LDAP enumeration bursts (hundreds of queries in seconds). MDI 'BloodHound reconnaissance' alert (built-in). Event 4662 volume spike. SMB NetSessionEnum RPC calls to many hosts. SIEM: LDAP query rate from workstation > baseline.
Processes performing local or domain account enumeration by invoking account directory queries or security APIs followed by structured output of account lists (DET0587/AN1612).
Suspicious shell commands or unauthorized access to /etc/passwd or /etc/shadow (AN1613).
Directory service queries or system utilities accessing account metadata stores, producing enumeration output (AN1614).
Cloud provider API calls where principals retrieve IAM users or roles in rapid succession (AN1615).
ESXi host account configuration or management APIs queried to retrieve user account listings (AN1617).
defense.artifacts: MDI alert: 'BloodHound reconnaissance' | DC Event 4662: bulk LDAP reads | SMB: NetSessionEnum RPC to many hosts | SharpHound .zip output on disk | Event 4104: Invoke-BloodHound / SharpHound | Network: LDAP+SMB burst from workstation
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| stats count by Account_Name, Client_Address
| where count>200

index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-BloodHound*" OR ScriptBlockText="*SharpHound*" OR ScriptBlockText="*CollectionMethod*")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4662
| summarize ldap_reads=count() by SubjectUserName, IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where ldap_reads > 200
| sort by ldap_reads desc
defense.prevention:
Deploy MDI. Block SharpHound binary via WDAC/AppLocker. Restrict NetSessionEnum (RestrictRemoteSam registry key). Restrict SAMR protocol to admin hosts. Enable Protected Users for sensitive accounts. Remediate excessive ACL permissions found by BloodHound.
Operating System Configuration: Prevent administrator account enumeration via UAC (GPO: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators).
User Account Management: Manage creation, modification, use, and permissions associated with user accounts.
defense.evasion: Use --throttle and --jitter to slow collection below burst thresholds. Collect from high-LDAP-volume host. Use targeted collection methods. Use ADExplorer or ldapsearch from Linux to avoid SharpHound signatures.
defense.misconfiguration: NetSessionEnum not restricted - any user can enumerate sessions. RestrictRemoteSam not configured. Excessive ACLs (GenericAll/GenericWrite on DA accounts by non-admin groups). MDI not deployed.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# RestrictRemoteSam not set (any auth user can enumerate local accounts):
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -EA SilentlyContinue).RestrictRemoteSam
# Returns $null = NOT restricted = VULNERABLE

# Dangerous ACE example:
Get-ObjectAcl 'Domain Admins' | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll'}
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict SAMR enumeration:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name RestrictRemoteSam -Value 'O:BAG:BAD:(A;;RC;;;BA)'

# Via GPO:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Local Policies → Security Options
# → Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM

# Remediate dangerous ACEs:
Remove-ADPermission -Identity 'DomainAdmin1' -User 'HelpDesk' -AccessRights GenericAll

# WDAC: deny SharpHound.exe by hash

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Runs the SharpHound collector to gather AD relationship data for BloodHound path analysis:
  Invoke-BloodHound       the SharpHound.ps1 collection function
  -CollectionMethod All   collect sessions, ACLs, group membership, trusts, delegation, etc.
  -OutputDirectory C:\Temp\   where to drop the zip
  -OutputPrefix 'crtp'    prefix for the output files
Import the resulting zip into BloodHound to see shortest paths to Domain Admin, unconstrained hosts, and ACL abuse edges.
